findings.description: `sandboxProfile`'s `writablePaths` doc still says the paths are fully symlink-resolved, but `writeProfile` now passes `grantPath` output: only the parent is resolved and the last name is kept as given, never followed. A future caller reading this seam could resolve a grant in full again and reopen the symlink-target grant that decision 108 closes.

The new 4-line call-site comment restates the rationale already in the JSDoc of grantPath (src/core/sandbox-profile.utils.ts, the seam the grant goes through): that a child can remove the grant or leave a symlink, and that the parent is resolved. AGENTS.md Comments: 'A WHY comment that restates the callee's JSDoc is a duplicate: read the callee's docs before keeping it; if the seam already says it, delete the call-site copy.' Trim it to the adapter-specific WHY (the holder is never granted, so no child can remove it) plus the decision 108 pointer.

Line 38 runs far past the ~100-column wrap used on every other line of this ADR and its siblings (0107, 0109). 'The parent is still followed, ... the toolchain cache key' was joined onto one long line, which looks like a mangled re-wrap. Re-wrap it to match the neighbouring lines (the docs/adr/README.md 'one file per decision' format has no stated width, so this is a style nit only).

The ceiling only names "the session's commit made an outer segment a link". Committed links that point outside the checkout are already refused at the cut, so the route that actually works is a gate child rewriting the segment at runtime. The ceiling should say so.

The `grantPath` JSDoc tells the story of the old bug and the incident (the `/var` versus `/private/var` mismatch, the failing vitest run) instead of just the contract: the parent is resolved, the name is appended unread, and a grant's parent must be one no child is granted. ADR 0108 already holds the rest.

ADR 0108 wording: "Main had the same hole" is ambiguous (branch or code path?); "the seam rule" is never defined (name `grantPath` instead); and "which the conductor has filed" gives no task id a reader can follow.

The file-wide `vi.mock('node:fs')` wraps `mkdirSync` for every test to serve one failure-path test, with no reset in `afterEach`, so a `mockImplementationOnce` left unconsumed would leak into the next `mkdirSync` call. Add a mock reset in `afterEach` to contain it.

A nested package's stage directory (`join(checkoutDir, pkg.dir)`) is granted through a parent inside the gate checkout. Earlier stages (build) and concurrent ones (lint, typecheck) can write that checkout, so a gate child can turn an outer segment of a multi-segment `pkg.dir` into a link at runtime, and `grantPath` follows it. This breaks grantPath's "parent never granted" invariant. It predates this PR: the old full resolve was strictly worse, and this PR narrows the problem.
